tasks.short: Verify installed HVAC systems against the green standard.

steps.what: Read the posted green standard for this system.
Verify heating and ventilating systems are designed, installed and calibrated.

tasks.design: The sheet metal worker still measures the installed heating, ventilating and air conditioning system on site and verifies that it is designed, installed and calibrated. A green standard line is already posted in the {DOCS}, with system, standard clause, required value, date and the author's name, so the hunt for that sheet is shorter. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The green standard sat on a paper sheet, so the worker hunted it before measuring the installed system.
tasks.enabler_now: The job file already holds a green standard line. Showing system, standard clause, required value, date and the author's name is configuration of that file.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the system is designed, installed and calibrated as the line requires is what the worker measures on site. A posted line does not measure it.
tasks.human_edge: The worker sees the installed system and refuses a line that does not name it.
tasks.altitude: The week is still the metal on site. Less time goes to hunting a standard sheet. The worker still measures and verifies.

reach.task: Post the green standard line before the visit.
reach.learn: The line needs system, standard clause, required value, date and the author's name, or the worker reads the paper sheet.

reach.task: Keep the standard clause current for this system.
reach.learn: The worker still verifies the installation. The assurer does not file a certificate from this check.

reach.task: Read the worker's on-site verification when asked.
reach.learn: The verification is what the worker measured. It is not a filed certificate.

evidence.claim: Measuring the installed system and verifying the design, installation and calibration stays with the sheet metal worker. A posted green standard line can be a shorter read. The on-site check itself is not shorter. Model knowledge.

For consequence class 1, the contractor and an independent quality assurer build the completion file the client submits, and contractors stay liable. This design does not assemble or send that file, and this on-site check is not that file.
GPS in company vans needs a legitimate interest, and tracking private use usually fails. This design does not track the worker or the van.
Hours, location and job logs per fitter observe presence and performance and need works-council consent. This design does not log the visit.
A system that allocates tasks based on individual behaviour or personal traits, or that evaluates worker performance, is high-risk. This design scores nobody.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task is only the on-site verification of one heating, ventilating and air conditioning system against the posted green standard. Fabricating, installing and soldering sit outside it. The design engineer or quality assurer posts the line before the visit.

Structured input: one green standard line in the {DOCS} with system, standard clause, required value, date and the author's name. If the line is missing or free text, the worker reads the paper sheet and that read is not shorter.

The worker still verifies on site. Nothing is recorded by a machine, sent, or committed. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. There is no commit and no send, so there is no gate on a sent version. The prior that reach is read-only is refused: confirming the installation is a write inside the organisation. The prior that the step acts outside the organisation is refused: verifying on site is not a send, this check does not file the green certificate, and it does not submit the completion file. The prior that a person must approve a sent version is refused: nothing is sent or committed.

A model is not used. The prior that a model is needed is refused: the worker has to measure the installed system. Existing system runtime is not the worker's time. The design does not log the visit and does not score the worker.
unknowns: Whether this firm's job file already has system, standard clause, required value, date and a name, or only a paper sheet.
Whether the client later asks for a certificate filing. This design does not file one.
research_questions: Who posts the green standard line, the design engineer or the quality assurer?
What share of visits start with no line the worker can read?

already_counted.description: Reading a missing or free-text standard sheet by hand, inside the remaining read.

incremental.description: Checking that the green standard line still names this system, clause, required value, date and an author.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the green standard line is often missing or free text, so the worker still hunts the paper sheet and the read is not shorter. High: most lines carry system, standard clause, required value, date and an author's name, and only that hunt shrinks. Measuring and verifying the installed system stay. The high stays under the net after the field check.
